alerts.title: TDF: creatinine rising, eGFR below 80
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF, and recommend substituting TDF with ABC if GFR is <60 mL/min. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL within 10 weeks of starting TDF, with eGFR now 78 mL/min/1.73m². TDF is a known cause of renal toxicity including chronic kidney disease and Fanconi syndrome. Evidence against drug attribution: pregnancy increases renal blood flow, which typically lowers creatinine; the rise is modest and eGFR remains above 60. However, the upward trend over just 10 weeks warrants close monitoring. Urinalysis is normal (no proteinuria), which argues against significant tubular damage.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue TDF but monitor creatinine and eGFR closely. If eGFR drops below 60 or creatinine continues rising, substitute TDF with ABC per guidelines.

alerts.title: Pregnant woman: VL due at 3 months on ART
alerts.message: Guidelines state that HIV-positive pregnant women newly initiated on ART at ANC should have a viral load test at 3 months on ART. Patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago (approximately 2.5 months), so the 3-month VL is not yet due but is imminent. The current VL of 89 copies/mL was presumably obtained early; guidelines specify the 3-month timepoint. No clinician plan was documented today, so it is unclear whether the 3-month VL has been scheduled. Ensuring timely VL monitoring is critical for this pregnant patient to confirm suppression and guide decisions about preventing vertical transmission.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule viral load test at 3 months on ART (approximately 2 weeks from now) per pregnancy-specific VL monitoring guidelines.

alerts.title: Cotrimoxazole preventive therapy missing
alerts.message: Guidelines prioritize cotrimoxazole preventive therapy (CPT) for all PLHIV newly initiating ART and for pregnant and breastfeeding women. Patient is both newly initiated on ART (10 weeks ago) and pregnant at 22 weeks, meeting two prioritized categories. CPT reduces risk of malaria, diarrhoea, pneumonia, hospitalization, and mortality. Patient is not currently on CPT and no plan to initiate it was documented. Note that additional intermittent preventive treatment for malaria using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine is not required for pregnant women already on CPT.

evidence.recommended_action: Initiate cotrimoxazole preventive therapy as patient qualifies under two prioritized categories: newly on ART and pregnant.

alerts.title: Mild anaemia with TDF renal trend
alerts.message: Guidelines list severe anaemia as a toxicity of AZT (Hb <8 mg/dL triggers substitution with TDF) and note that TDF can cause Fanconi syndrome. Patient's Hb is 10.8 g/dL, which is mildly low for pregnancy (physiological anaemia of pregnancy is common). TDF is not a direct cause of anaemia, but if TDF needs to be substituted due to declining renal function, AZT would be contraindicated as the alternative if anaemia worsens. Current Hb does not meet the <8 g/dL threshold for action. Iron supplementation with ferrous sulfate is already prescribed, which is appropriate management for pregnancy-related anaemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor Hb alongside renal function. If TDF substitution becomes necessary, choose ABC rather than AZT given the low-normal Hb.
